Answer: A
Reason: Figure 1b demonstrates a marked rightward displacement and rotation of the cardiac silhouette into the right hemithorax compared to the more central position in Figure 1a, which is characteristic of acute cardiac herniation through a pericardial defect following pneumonectomy or major pleural surgery. This mechanical complication explains the patient's acute haemodynamic compromise due to torsion of the great vessels.
